_comment: The PHENOMENA register: the completeness authority for the reactor PHYSICS, the twin of equipment-register.json. Mission rule: nothing is guessed, and nothing is silently omitted. Every phenomenon a real RBMK-1000 exhibits must appear here, with a source and a status. The reason it exists: an item the Director did not name must not silently vanish. For equipment the risk was a missing machine; for physics the risk is a missing FEEDBACK or TRANSIENT - the reactor then LOOKS right and BEHAVES wrong, which is the failure the xenon-readout bug already demonstrated (xenon was displayed but never entered the neutron balance). Status is one of: modelled (coupled into the neutron/thermal balance, and a self-test measures it), readout (computed and displayed, but NOT coupled - it cannot change k_eff), named-only (described in a source, not yet built), unsourced (expected to exist but with no source found - MUST be resolved or explicitly justified as absent). The spine source is INSAG-7 section 2 (the design features that 'had a primary influence on the course of the accident'), plus the Soviet operating regulation (Reglament 1E-S-II, 1983) and NUREG-1250. The gate is PhenomenaRegister.summary(): it prints the counts so 'is anything missing?' cannot be quietly zero.

_statusLegend.modelled: Coupled into the neutron/thermal balance (or a live plant action); a self-test measures it.
_statusLegend.readout: Computed and DISPLAYED but NOT coupled — cannot change k_eff. This is the xenon failure mode; a bug.
_statusLegend.blocked_on_data: Built and ready to couple, but the required data cannot be obtained with the current library/toolchain. Recorded so it cannot be forgotten.
_statusLegend.named_only: Described in a source, not built.
_statusLegend.unsourced: Expected to exist, no source found — MUST be resolved or justified absent.

items.note: Two-group diffusion on the 250 mm lattice; the flux is the state.
Gives the reactor its controllable period.

items.name_en: Void coefficient of reactivity (steam in the channel)
items.note: POSITIVE. The dominant feedback. Derived from the channel energy balance; magnitude anchored to INSAG-7 +0.020 via xsec.void_worth_scale.

items.where: ChannelCooling.coolantTempC (per node) + FuelTemperature.anchoredToPeak -> fuelTempByNode -> RbmkXsec.fuelCell(.., fuelTemp, ..)
items.note: NEGATIVE, prompt. The one feedback that opposes the void. The fuel temperature is now DERIVED per axial node (coolant temp + anchored conduction rise), not a fitted scalar: the fuel is hot where the flux is, and it tracks coolant flow and inlet temperature, so a pump trip cools it. Was T=640+600*(P-1) with both constants unregistered.

items.source: INSAG-7 2.4 (startup free of xenon); Xenon model
items.note: NEGATIVE, slow. Was READOUT-ONLY until 2026-11-15 - it did not touch k_eff. Now enters the fuel cell thermal absorption (sigma_Xe*N_Xe_eq). Measured: 3x ratio moves keff by -0.0227.

POSITIVE and slow. The SIGN is derived (openmc/rbmk_graphite_mgxs.py: +1.17e-5/degC). The coupling is BUILT: graphiteTempC -> RbmkGraphiteTemp.apply -> RbmkXsec.fuelCell. It does not fire because RbmkGraphiteTemp.matchesLattice() is true only for the OpenMC lattice table, and the shipped table is the ROSFOND/1-D one. The slope is a FRACTIONAL change of the OpenMC cell's constants, so applying it to a different table flips the sign — the gate is correct, not a bug. To unblock: produce the temperature sweep from the ROSFOND cell, which needs MF=7 thermal scattering (S(a,b)) for carbon at several temperatures. The repo has NO S(a,b) path (no MF=7 reader, no thermal files), so this cannot be derived from ROSFOND as the toolchain stands. Blocked on data, not on code.
NOT a separate fitted term: it is the sum of the feedbacks above, as INSAG-7 defines it. A fitted POWER_COEFF term was removed from reactivity() so the readout is physical.

items.name_en: Positive scram (graphite displacer at the channel bottom)
items.where: rod geometry in RbmkSolver3D (bottom-peaked axial shape)
items.note: The 1.25 m water gap under the displacer. Inserting a fully withdrawn rod first ADDS reactivity low in the core. Measured in NoAccidentModeSelfTest: k rises 1.10255 -> 1.10793 over rod 0.00 -> 0.20. Derived from geometry, NOT the fitted RodWorth.bottomPeaked() curve.
The ~18 s full insertion; fast enough that the displacer effect and the absorber fight.

items.name_en: Spatial power distribution and rod interference
items.note: The core is 11.8 m across and only loosely coupled; local perturbations stay local. Modelled by the 3-D solve, but the AR/rod-bank shadowing is NOT yet per-rod.

items.name_en: Operating reactivity margin (ORM) and its limit
items.where: UnifiedReactorCore.orm() -> RodBank.orm(); limits in provenance orm.reference
items.note: The reactivity left if every rod were withdrawn, in 'equivalent fully-inserted manual rods' (SKALA request K0S0000). BUILT and measured by OrmSelfTest (36 checks): RodBank sums the individual rods' worths from the cartogram, and the limits are sourced (provenance orm.reference: nominal 45-48, warning 43, limit 30, from the SKALA walkthrough and Reglament 1E-S-II 9). This is an operational quantity derived FROM the rod state, not a reactivity feedback, so 'coupled to k_eff' is the wrong test for it — the rod state is already in the neutron balance. ENFORCEMENT is a separate phenomenon (orm.limit_enforcement) and it is missing.

items.name_en: ORM limit enforcement (warning at 43, prohibition at 30)
items.note: A real unit is bound by the regulation's ORM limits: «не менее 26÷30 стержней» at nominal, below 26 only with the chief engineer's permission, and «при снижении … до 15 стержней реактор должен быть немедленно заглушен». Now ENFORCED as an ALARM: RodBank.margin() classifies the live margin into NOMINAL (>=26) / PERMISSION_ONLY (<26) / SHUTDOWN_REQUIRED (<=15), and /rbmk status prints the band, red at SHUTDOWN_REQUIRED. It is deliberately an alarm and NOT a lockout: the regulation forbids the action, the machinery does not physically stop the operator, and unit 4 was run at ~8 rods with nothing stopping it. OrmSelfTest checks the bands land on the regulation's values. CAVEAT: the ORM SCALE is currently ~1.6x high (a plausible operating point reads 47 rods, not 26-30) — see provenance orm.scale_calibration; the limits are right, the rod-worth calibration is not. What is still missing is the annunciation PANEL — that is plant.alarm_panel.

items.name_en: Annunciation panel (SKALA alarms as lamps, not chat text)
items.source: SKALA; the operator interface described in the walkthrough
items.note: Real alarms appear on an annunciator panel with a lamp and a horn per setpoint. Here every alarm is a line of chat text, so an operator can miss it, and there is no horn. The ORM bands, the trip reasons and the level alarms all exist as values but have no physical annunciation. This is what makes 'the operator was warned' true in a way a worker would recognise.
The scram drives the rods in; the accident then follows from physics. There is NO accident mode (NoAccidentModeSelfTest).
A plain integral regulator on the power error.

items.name_en: Forced channel flow, subcooling and boiling onset
items.where: ChannelCooling (energy balance up the flux shape)
items.note: The void is derived from this, not fitted. Subcooling matters for stability.

items.name_en: Pump cavitation on loss of subcooling
items.note: If subcooling falls to near zero, the pumps can cavitate and lose flow. Not modelled; the plant throttles pumps but there is no cavitation.
Flow driven by the density difference when the pumps stop. Not modelled; flow is a set value.

items.name_en: Critical heat flux / dryout of a channel
items.note: A channel that boils dry overheats and can rupture. Not modelled; there is no CHF limit on the channel.
The heat that cannot be switched off; drives the post-scram thermal state.

items.name_en: Graphite heating and its slow time constant
items.note: Computed with a slow time constant (TAU_GRAPHITE) and fed to the graphite feedback. Blocked for the same reason as feedback.graphite: the value is computed but cannot reach k_eff until the lattice/graphite-slope pair matches. Not displayed to the operator, so it is not a misleading readout — it is a dead internal quantity awaiting its data.
The loosely coupled core can oscillate in power distribution. Xenon is coupled but uniform (one ratio), so axial/radial xenon oscillation is NOT modelled.

items.name_en: Fuel burnup / depletion of reactivity margin with time
items.note: A fresh core has a very different ORM from a burnt one. Not modelled; the lattice is fixed.
The other, slower poison. Not modelled; only xenon is.

items.name_en: Protection trips: separator level, low feedwater, loss of two MCPs
items.note: Raises АЗ-5 on: high/low separator level, feedwater flow to 0.75 of CURRENT, loss of two MCPs on one side. Each reads live plant state and ACTS (scram drops the rods and trips the pumps), so this is genuinely coupled. The feedwater item was FIXED this session: it was an absolute 10% of nominal (a different protection, firing far too late); it is now the regulation's АЗ-1 rate-of-drop trip «до 0,75 текущего» (ГЛАВА 3 item 2), held against a trailing 60 s window so a slow ramp does not trip it. Measured: a fall to 70% trips, a fall to 80% does not (PlantSelfTest).

items.source: Reglament 1E-S-II (setpoint to be read from the regulation)
items.note: The regulation has NO single '104% overpower' trip. Its power protection is TWO protections (ГЛАВА 3, АЗ-5): a RATE trip — «уменьшение периода разгона до 10±2 сек при мощности до 160 мВт(т) … и до 20 сек в остальном диапазоне» — and a MARGIN trip — «повышение уровня мощности на 0,5% Nном» below 5% power, «на 10% Nном над заданным» in the 5-100% range. NEITHER is implemented in checkTrips, so in AccidentSequence the unit runs up with no automatic protection at all. This is the most important missing trip: it is the one that would have caught the runaway. Setpoints now SOURCED (provenance trip.az1_az5_setpoints), so this is buildable — it is no longer blocked on data, only on implementation.

The regulation gives the setpoint: «повышение давления в реакторном пространстве до аварийной уставки – 0,15 кгс/см2» (ГЛАВА 3, АЗ-5 item з), plus «повышение давления в барабан-сепараторах до 75 кгс/см2 (абсолютного)» (item о). Neither is implemented — the separator pressure in the model drifts to a setpoint and never trips. Now SOURCED (provenance trip.az1_az5_setpoints), so buildable.
The 12 x 25 m3 accumulators. Not modelled as an active injection.
The 3200 m3 bubbler pool that condenses a steam release. Named in the equipment register; no steam-release physics drives it.
The consequence path. A radiology layer exists elsewhere, but it is not driven by a core-damage model.
The days-long graphite fire that dispersed the inventory. Not modelled.
